relations.quote: The layer performs the butterfly rounds of [Synthetic polynomial transforms](synthetic-transforms.md), which otherwise needs one whole-array pass per butterfly.
The layer gets its exponent from [Recursive power saving from s<Wm](recursive-power-saving.md), which turns such a recursion into a power saving.
The layer moves whole chunks by [Fast interchange of address fields](fast-address-interchange.md) to realize its binary basis changes.

relations.quote: This single truncation keeps error within the bound of [Fixed-point precision and exact recovery](fixed-point-precision.md), which needs error below $1/2$.

symbols.name: selected chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected address chunks, which counts the chunks the layer acts on.
symbols.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the number of selected address chunks, and let $d$ be an upper bound on $\Delta$, so $\Delta\le d$.

symbols.name: chunk bound
symbols.meaning: An upper bound on the number of selected address chunks, which counts the chunks.
symbols.quote: Let $\Delta$ be the number of selected address chunks, and let $d$ be an upper bound on $\Delta$, so $\Delta\le d$.

symbols.name: chunk bit count
symbols.meaning: The number of consecutive address bits in one chunk.
symbols.quote: Each chunk consists of $\chi$ consecutive address bits, and the selected bit sits at one common offset in every chunk.

symbols.name: layer exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the layer cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$.
symbols.quote: The layer costs $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a fixed exponent $\lambda'<1$, where $V$ is the stored bit volume.

symbols.name: bit-flip matrix
symbols.meaning: The $2\times 2$ matrix that swaps the two basis states of one bit.

symbols.name: phase matrix
symbols.meaning: The diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,i)$ that multiplies the imaginary part by $i$.

symbols.name: two-point kernel
symbols.meaning: The $2\times 2$ matrix $\tfrac12((1+i)I+(1-i)Y)$, whose tensor powers the layer computes.

symbols.name: child-call count
symbols.meaning: The number of child calls into which one call on a group of $mf$ selected bits is reduced.
symbols.quote: The phase identities for $\Xi$ reduce this group to $\Psi$ child calls, each computing $\Xi^{\otimes f}$ on one slot, with $\Psi<Wm$.

symbols.name: fixed exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent $1-2^{-50}$ that bounds $\Psi/W$ by a power of $m$.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponent $\sigma=1-2^{-50}$ gives $\Psi/W<m^{\sigma}$, because $\Psi/W$ is $m$ times one minus a tiny fraction.

symbols.name: normalized cost
symbols.meaning: The time of a call on $f$ selected bits divided by the volume it works on.
symbols.quote: With $T(f)$ the normalized cost (time divided by volume), each child costs $(V/W)\,T(f)$, and the node's outside work is $O(V\chi^{\tau})$ for its chunk exchanges, with $\tau<1$, plus linear copying.

symbols.name: butterfly map
symbols.meaning: The map $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ applied to a pair of records, coefficientwise.
symbols.quote: Fast simultaneous butterfly layers is a fixed-tape procedure that applies $H_0(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2)$ to one bit position in several address chunks at once.
